questions.q:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
Though the / global financial crisis, / China's economy continues / to grow at an impressive rate.

(SSC Steno 2024 T-1 : 11 Dec Shift-2)
o: to grow at an impressive rate.
china's economy continues
Though the
global financial crisis,
questions.s:
Correct Answer: - "Though the".

Explanation:

  • The main grammatical problem in the sentence lies in the use of “though” without a complete clause following it.

  • “Though” must introduce a full statement that shows contrast, which is missing here.

  • To make the sentence grammatically correct, “though” should be replaced with “despite”, which can be followed by a noun phrase.

  • Hence, the error appears in the first part of the sentence.

Corrected Sentence:
Despite the global financial crisis, China’s economy continues to grow at an impressive rate.

questions.q: Which collective noun is correctly matched with its group?
o: A bunch of soldiers
A pride of lions
A herd of fish
questions.s: "A pride of lions" is the correct collective noun for a group of lions. Option (a) should be "a collection of books" (library is a place, not a collective noun). Option (b) should be "a troop of soldiers" (bunch is for grapes, flowers, keys). Option (d) should be "a school of fish" or "a shoal of fish" (herd is for cattle, elephants, deer).

questions.s:

questions.q: The traditional inn was built of stones, providing shelter to weary travelers on their journeys.
o: to weary travelers on their journeys
questions.s:
The correct term is "built of stone" instead of "built of stones." "Stone" is an uncountable noun when used in the context of building materials. Therefore, it should not be pluralized as "stones."

Therefore, the corrected sentence would be: "The traditional inn was built of stone, providing shelter to weary travelers on their journeys."

questions.q: At the edge of the meadow, a dense herd of trees marked the boundary between civilization and the untamed wilderness beyond.
questions.s:
"A dense clump of trees" - This option is the most appropriate. "Clump" is commonly used to describe a small, dense grouping of objects, such as trees in this case. It accurately conveys the image of a concentrated mass of trees at the edge of the meadow.

"a dense fleet of trees" - The word "fleet" typically refers to a group of ships or vehicles, not trees. So, this option doesn't accurately describe the arrangement of trees at the edge of the meadow.

"a dense crew of trees" - Similarly, "crew" usually refers to a group of people working together, such as on a ship or in a team. It doesn't fit well with describing trees.

questions.q:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

My two ________ came to visit us during the long holiday weekend.
questions.s:
The context of the sentence mentions "two" people, indicating that a plural noun is needed. The blank requires the correct plural form of the compound noun 'brother-in-law'.

The correct option is "brothers-in-law". For compound nouns of this type, the plural is formed by adding '-s' to the principal or main noun, which is 'brother'.

The other options are incorrect: "brother-in-laws" incorrectly pluralizes the last word; "brothers'-in-law" is an incorrect plural possessive form; and "brother-in-law's" is a singular possessive form.

Thus, the complete sentence is: "My two brothers-in-law came to visit us during the long holiday weekend."

Hence, option (c) is the correct answer.

Correct Sentence: The snowstorm will affect thousands of travellers.

o: He inherited a

his wealthy uncle

questions.s:
When a definite numeral adjective is added before the following nouns, they take a singular form. E.g.: Pair, score, gross, stone, hundred, dozen, thousand, million, billion, etc.

    • "a billion dollar" is incorrect because "dollar" should be plural ("dollars") when referring to a large amount of money.
    • The correct phrase should be "a billion dollars" instead.

Therefore, the corrected sentence would be: "He inherited a billion dollars from his wealthy uncle."

questions.q: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
o: He has been looking
for an interesting work
for a long time
No error
questions.s:
Solution

Work is an uncountable noun. Hence use of definite article AN is wrong with it. The correct usage will be - An interesting Piece of work.
Concept - "A" and "an" are indefinite articles used to modify singular countable nouns. Uncountable nouns, also known as mass nouns, do not have a plural form and cannot be counted, so they do not use "a" or "an".

questions.q:
Parts of the following sentence have been underlined and given as options. Select the option that contains an error.

My brother-in-laws who live in Mumbai have decided to come and stay with us for a week.
questions.s:
The error is in the plural form of the compound noun "brother-in-law". In compound nouns of this type (noun + preposition + noun), the plural is formed by adding '-s' to the principal or main noun, which is 'brother' in this case. Therefore, the correct plural form is "brothers-in-law". The verb 'have' is a plural verb, which is correct as the intended subject is plural.

The correct sentence is: My brothers-in-law who live in Mumbai have decided to come and stay with us for a week.

Hence, option (d) is the correct answer.

questions.q:
The following sentence has been divided into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error.

The factory owner / has bought some new / expensive machineries / for the upcoming project.
questions.s:
The error lies in the usage of the word "machineries". The word "machinery" is an uncountable noun, which means it refers to a group or collection of machines as a whole. Uncountable nouns do not have a plural form. Therefore, adding an '-s', '-es' or '-ies' is incorrect. The correct term is "machinery".

Correct sentence: The factory owner has bought some new expensive machinery for the upcoming project.

So, there is an error in the part mentioned in option c).

Hence, option (c) is the answer.

Note: Countable and uncountable nouns: 1. Countable nouns are the class of nouns that can be counted, for example, 'table' - one table, two tables, three tables, etc. 2. Uncountable nouns are the nouns that cannot be counted or usually are not counted, for example, light, water, milk, information, furniture, etc. They do not generally have a plural form and can't be preceded by 'a' or 'an'. Many abstract nouns are typically uncountable. Some uncountable nouns can be used in the plural as well, depending on the meaning or context of the word.

The ‘noun’ that comes after ‘one of the’ must be plural. So, ‘one of the finest steaks’ is the correct form.

Therefore, the correct sentence would be: “This restaurant is known for serving one of the finest steaks in town.”

questions.q: Raj surprised everyone (1) when he created an unbreakable record (2)/ of one and a half centuries.(3)/ No error (4)
questions.s: Replace 'one and a half centuries' with 'one and a half century' or 'a century and a half'. In fractions with "one and a half," the noun remains singular: "one and a half century."

questions.q:
In the following question, one part of the sentence may have an error. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option.

The company has premises with a total (A)/ area of 15 hectares, of which 3600 square metres are (B)/ a workshop and a staff of 15,200 (C)/ who are qualified technicians. (D)
questions.s:
Part B has an error. In the given sentence, '3600 square metres' refers to a specific amount of area. When a plural noun denotes a specific amount, length, quantity considered as a whole, the verb is generally singular. So, the verb 'are' should be replaced with its singular form 'is' to rectify the given sentence.

Hence, option (d) is the correct answer.

The correct sentence is: The company has premises with a total area of 15 hectares, of which 3600 square metres is a workshop and a staff of 15,200 who are qualified technicians.
